Classical comparative-method kernels

Source: R/kernels.R
classical-kernels.Rd

Each function returns one kernel component. Components are combined with +, e.g. k_bm() + k_white(). Every component has its own scale parameter sigma; its contribution to the covariance is sigma^2 times the base kernel below (t_ij: shared path length from the root to the most recent common ancestor of tips i and j; d_ij: patristic distance; T: tree height).

Usage

k_bm()

k_lambda(lower = 1e-07, upper = 1)

k_kappa(lower = 1e-06, upper = 1)

k_delta(lower = 1e-05, upper = 3)

k_eb(lower = function(ti, cmp) -log(1e+06)/ti$Tmax, upper = 0)

k_ou(
  root = c("random", "fixed"),
  lower = function(ti, cmp) 1e-07/ti$Tmax,
  upper = function(ti, cmp) 50/ti$Tmax
)

k_white(df = NULL)

Arguments

lower, upper

Bounds of the kernel parameter. They may be numbers or functions of the tree information (see tree_info()); the defaults match those of phylolm.

root

For k_ou(), "random" (stationary) or "fixed" root.

df

For k_white(): degrees of freedom of a Student-t residual (heavy tails, robust to outlying species). NULL (default) gives Gaussian residuals. The t residual is a scale mixture: each species gets a latent variance multiplier with an inverse-gamma(df/2, df/2) prior, so the model needs method = "sample".

Value

A kernel component.

Details

  • k_bm(): Brownian motion, t_ij.

  • k_lambda(): Pagel's lambda. Internal branches are multiplied by lambda and tip branches lengthened to keep tip heights fixed.

  • k_kappa(): Pagel's kappa, every branch length raised to kappa.

  • k_delta(): Pagel's delta, node heights transformed, giving T^(1 - delta) t_ij^delta.

  • k_eb(): early burst / ACDC, rate exp(rate * t), giving (exp(rate * t_ij) - 1) / rate.

  • k_ou(): Ornstein-Uhlenbeck with selection strength alpha; random (stationary) root exp(-alpha d_ij) / (2 alpha), or fixed root, which multiplies this by 1 - exp(-2 alpha t_ij). On ultrametric trees it is fitted in branch-wise form (O(N)); on other trees through its dense closed form.

  • k_white(): independent tip variance (residual, within-species variation); k_bm() + k_white() is Pagel's lambda on an ultrametric tree.

Examples

k_bm() + k_white()
#> phylogp kernel: bm() + white() 
#>   bm1        bm()                         parameters: sigma
#>   white1     white()                      parameters: sigma
k_ou(root = "fixed")
#> phylogp kernel: ou(root = "fixed") 
#>   ou1        ou(root = "fixed")           parameters: sigma, alpha
